description: Contract cases for the field controller's REST API v1 (controller/atalaia_controller/api.py; the Android controller, app/lib/controller/controller_api.dart, decision PE24). Each case starts a fresh controller (no games, node id 0, a radio that is up, a clock at 0) and runs its steps in order. A 'request' step sends method and path with the token named (gm, read, none: no Authorization header, bad: an unknown token) and the JSON body if given; the answer must have the status and, if given, a body matching 'json'. 'save' keeps values of the answer (dotted paths) under names; '${name}' in a path or as a whole string value stands for a saved value. An 'rx' step is a decrypted packet from a box as the radio gives it (HELLO, STATE: the payload's fields by name, counters by team id; EVENT: the event, encoded by the core's codec, prio from the schema when not given). An 'advance_ms' step moves the controller's clock on and runs its tick once. Stream steps (WS /api/v1/stream, added with slice S2 of PE24): 'ws_connect' opens a connection under a name with the token named ('via': 'query', the default, puts it in ?token=, 'header' in Authorization), and the first message must match 'hello', or, with 'close', the controller must close it with that code before any message; 'ws' takes every message that connection got since its last 'ws' step (the runner publishes a marker {'type': 'pong', 'sentinel': n} through the stream after them and drops the markers), and they must match 'messages' as a list, so nothing may come in between or be missing; 'ws_send' sends 'json' and the next message must match 'reply'; 'ws_flood' hands 'count' messages {'type': 'system', 'kind': 'test', 'i': i} to every open connection at once, before any is sent, and the controller must close the connection named with code 'close' (a client more than 'stream_max_queue' messages behind, a case setting: 256 when not given). An 'mqtt' step takes every message the controller published to its MQTT broker since the last 'mqtt' step, as {'topic', 'qos', 'retain', 'payload' (the JSON payload)}, and they must match the list given. 'mqtt_acl' lists who may read and write which topics. A 'restart' step (added with slice S3) stops the controller and starts a new one on the same store, as after a reboot or a crash: the clock goes on, the open stream connections end (a 'ws_connect' after it opens one to the new controller), the MQTT messages go on to the same list. A case may set 'persist_game_key' (true when not given: decision OT-7), the controller's setting for the whole case, before and after its restarts. Radio steps (added with slice S4): an 'rx' step may set 'ack': true (the packet asks for an ACK); 'tx' takes everything the controller asked of its radio since the last 'tx' step, in order, and it must match the list given ('kinds' keeps only those kinds): a packet is {'kind': its message type (HELLO, EVENT, ACK, STATE, CMD, TIME...), 'source', 'seq', 'hop_limit', 'prio' (telemetry, normal, critical), 'ack' (an ACK requested), 'fields': the payload by the field names of protocol/schema/messages.yaml, bytes in hex}; the modem's commands are {'kind': 'configure', 'game_id', 'node_id', 'epoch', 'max_hops', 'channel_hz'} (the key is never shown), {'kind': 'clear'}, {'kind': 'channel', 'channel_hz'} and {'kind': 'peer_epochs', 'epochs': {node id: epoch}}. 'radio_state' ('up' or 'down') is the modem's link going down or coming back; 'tx_ack' {'seq', 'status'} is the modem's TX_ACK. Joins (slice S4): a case may set 'join_key' (the field join key, hex; none when not given: joins are refused with 503); a 'join_decode' step opens the join text given (usually a saved one) with it and its fields (protocol/join.md's names, bytes in hex) must match 'json'; 'save' works as for a request. Android props on Wi-Fi (WS /api/v1/prop, protocol/prop-link.md; slice S4): 'prop_connect' opens a link under a name for 'node_id' with the game key 'key' (hex, usually a saved join_decode's) to the game 'game_id' (the saved ${gid} when not given): the runner answers the challenge with the proof, and the first message must match 'welcome', or, with 'close', the messages until the controller closes it must match 'messages' and the close code 'close'; 'prop_send' sends 'json' on a link; 'prop' takes every message the link got since its last look (the runner sends a ping after them and stops at its pong), which must match 'messages'; 'prop_closed' takes the messages until the controller closes the link, which must match 'messages', and its close code 'close'. Check-in and positions (slice S5): every controller has field check-in and player positions set up, with no field CA (HTTPS off: the poster has no text), the privacy notice version 1, the portugal limit template and the default check-in settings; its wall clock starts at 'wall_start' (Unix seconds) and moves with the clock, and the field's day is in UTC. A request or 'ws_connect' step may give 'bearer', a token to send as it is (usually a saved player token, '${ptok}') instead of a named one; 'ws_closed' takes every message a connection gets until the controller closes it, which must match 'messages', and its close code 'close'. The chrono readings in the cases are signed with a fixed test key (Ed25519, seed bytes 0 to 31; its public key is the one the cases register). Matching: an object matches when every key given matches (other keys are free); '$absent' as a value means the key must not be there and '$any' that it must be there; a list matches element by element and must have the same length, except {'$contains': [...]}, where each pattern must match some element. The Python controller is the reference: these cases describe what it does (controller/tests/test_api_contract.py), and the Android controller must do the same (app/test/controller/api_contract_test.dart).

field_and_radio.description: Slice S7a of PE24 (decisions PE24-74 to PE24-79): the field plan (field images and floor plans per level, the levels, each plan's map position, the map features with their visibility, the field from a map, the boxes' places) and the field's radio channel with its noise scan, on both controllers. Run after 'cases' with the same rules, and these additions. A request may give 'raw' instead of 'body': {'content_type', 'base64'} sent as the raw body with that Content-Type, zero bytes appended up to 'size' when given (an uploaded image). A request step may check 'content_type' (the answer's media type, without parameters) and 'body_base64' (the answer's bytes); an answer is read as JSON only when it is application/json. Every controller keeps its field plan across a 'restart'. The radio answers each MEASURE (the noise scan) with the noise the case set: a 'noise' step gives, per channel in Hz, [the 90th percentile in dBm, LoRa preambles detected in 10 tries] (a channel not given: -118 dBm and none; the minimum is 6 dB below the 90th percentile, the mean 3, the median 4, the maximum 9 above, the samples as many as the dwell's milliseconds); 'tx' shows each as {'kind': 'measure', 'channel_hz', 'dwell_ms'}. 'hold_measure' makes measurements wait (the scan stays running) and 'scan_wait' lets them go and waits until the scan has ended. A 'tx' step whose 'tx' is '$any' only empties the list.

cases.name: whoami: the radio and field areas both controllers serve (slice S7a)
field plan: the image, its limits, its map position, the stream and a restart
field levels: a plan and a map position per level, the boxes' places, fewer levels
map features: types, shapes, the boundary, each token's view on REST and the stream
the field from a map: plan, map position and boundary at once, per level
the radio channel: the choice, a game's channel, the noise scan, cancelling it
tokens: none, unknown, read and GM
whoami: the console's areas both controllers serve (features, decision PE24-70)
the modes this controller runs
a Domination game from creation to its end
Hold-All's field.lua scores while one team holds every box
Last Stand's field.lua ends the game when the defenders fall
a game ends by itself at its time limit
the read token never sees gm_only parameters or event data
requests the controller refuses
the stream: tokens, the hello snapshot and ping
the stream follows a game in order, gm_only data for the GM token only
a stream client that falls behind is dropped and catches up with a new hello
MQTT: the topics and payloads of a game
MQTT: gm_only event data never reaches the broker
a restart keeps the live game: its clock, score, nodes and log
the GM's score adjustments outlive two restarts
field.lua runs again after a restart and its earlier points stay
without persist_game_key a restart loses the key and the game can only be ended
the radio: the game on the modem, the controller's packets and ACKs
the radio after a restart: a new epoch under the same game key
joins: payloads sealed with the field join key, one node id per device
an Android prop on Wi-Fi: the proof, its packets, TIME and commands
check-in: the poster, open games, a player token and what it may read
check-in: declarations, the GM's changes, a stale token, removal and leaving
chrono: a marshal's signed readings pass and refuse declarations
the player stream: its own check-in, names for staff only, 4409 after a change
positions: who sees whom, the level kept, a team's view for a while, gone at the end
check-ins, tokens, readings and positions outlive a restart
a VIP's GPS reports reach field.lua: VIP / Payload's extraction ends the game

mqtt_acl.description: Who may read and write which topics on the controller's MQTT broker: the Pi's Mosquitto ACL (controller/deploy/atalaia.acl, checked by controller/tests/test_api_contract.py) and the Android controller's embedded broker (app/lib/controller/mqtt_broker.dart, MqttAcl.field, checked by app/test/controller/api_contract_test.dart). Users: 'gm' (GM tools: reads everything, publishes commands), 'reader' (scoreboards: events, score and nodes) and 'controller' (the field controller itself). A user not listed may do nothing.
